ms.promise:
・Minswap V2 Smart Contract code built on Aiken will undergo an audit by TxPipe, the company that built the Aiken programming language. 
・During the audit process TxPipe will make recommendations on how to address the vulnerabilities identified during the audit process. The vulnerabilities include scenarios where a malicious actor might exploit the validator to disrupt the platform or its users. The Audit Report will include: 
・A) A Title for each of the Findings
・B) The severity assessment of each Finding (Critical, Minor, Info)
・C) Status (Resolved/Unresolved).
ms.criteria:
・The audit will be publicly announced in December by both Minswap Labs and TxPipe to be accountable to the community that it is in fact ongoing.
・The Audit process and the finding and addressing of vulnerabilities will be completed within the month of December. The Audit Report will be released as soon as the process concludes. The Audit Report will highlighting any findings or concerns, their status and a high level overview of the contracts behavior.
ms.report:
・It was decided to switch the first audit company from TxPipe to CertiK due to internal planning issues. 
・Link to an article posted on Medium will be provided to demonstrate the join announcement of Minswap V2 Audit process commencement by Minswap Labs and CertiK
・Link to the Audit Report by CertiK (this report is not yet the version to be shared with the public). 
・The Audit Report has been updated now since the last submission.
・That being said, in the CertiK audit process, Issues will have tag "minor", "major" and "critical". CertiK addresses not only potential issues, but also other types such as "information", "potential optimization", ...Only issues can result in vulnerabilities, other kind of findings (such as the ones you mentioned in the POA rejection) are marked acknowledged instead of making any changes since they cannot lead to vulnerabilities.
